DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: Rows of piles under the pier deck, each one furred with growth and ringed by the shadows of the planks above.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Pier Piling Forest

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A steel ladder bolted to the pier's landward face — the surface-supplied crews' way in and out.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Pier Ladder

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A scatter of rounded boulders on bright sand, the first thing a new diver learns to navigate around.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Shelf Boulder Garden

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A stock anchor half buried in the sand, a favourite turning mark for the shelf swim.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: The Old Anchor

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The line where the sand gives way to swaying grass, staked with the survey transect's end markers.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Eelgrass Meadow Edge

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: Gridded transplant plots pegged out in the meadow, each corner flagged for the monitoring divers.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Eelgrass Nursery Plots

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A ridge of sand built where the marsh channel drops its load, shifting a little with every big tide.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Marsh Mouth Sandbar

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A buoyed line across the channel mouth that drift surveys follow with the ebb.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Marsh Drift Line

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The tallest stand in the forest, where the stipes rise like columns and the canopy closes overhead.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Kelp Cathedral

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A rock ledge at the forest's edge where the kelp holdfasts grip and the photo quadrats are laid.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Holdfast Ledge

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A graduated post standing on the flats, its face read by every survey team on the way out.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Tide Gauge Post

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A weighted mooring with a water-quality sonde clipped to its riser, serviced on a schedule the crew holds.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Sonde Mooring

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The ported end of an outfall pipe on its rock apron, the discharge zone flagged on every dive plan.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Outfall Diffuser

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The buried-and-exposed run of pipe leading out to the diffuser, marked with stakes along its length.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Outfall Pipe Run

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A line of buoy moorings whose chains drop from the surface at the channel's western approach.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Approach Buoy Chain

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The moorings of the channel markers, each chain rising out of sight to a lit buoy overhead.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Channel Marker Chain

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: Hollow concrete domes in tidy rows, set out on the bottom for the monitoring programme.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Reef Ball Rows

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A steel rack of tiles left on the bottom for whatever settles, photographed on a schedule the crew holds.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Settlement Tile Rack

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A concrete mooring block sunk in the mud, its chain the only fixed thing on the plain.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Mud Plain Mooring Block

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The upright bow of an old workboat hull in the hollow, its rail still readable under the growth.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: The Wreck's Bow

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The hull's stern, settled deeper in the scour, where the survey photo line ends.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: The Wreck's Stern

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The edge where the mud plain drops away into the dark — the turnaround point on most dive plans.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Trench Lip

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A stacked-stone marker on the trench floor left by the ROV crews as a survey datum.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Trench Floor Cairn

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: The mount's top, in brighter water, ringed by the transect pins of the capstone survey.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Seamount Pinnacle

DEEP_LANDMARKS.blurb: A dip between the pinnacle and a lower shoulder where the ascent line to the surface is set.
DEEP_LANDMARKS.name: Seamount Saddle
